claims.text: Two pages: A links only to B; B links equally to A and B. Teleport is uniform with probability 0.2. What is B’s stationary share? Options: 35.7%; 50%; 64.3%. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.

claims.text: A two-state chain switches A→B with probability 0.6 and B→A with 0.3. Stationary B share? Flow balance gives B=0.6/(0.6+0.3)=2/3.

provenance.difference: New teaching boundary: Random surfer. Existing boundary: The learner can explain that a random surfer who follows links and jumps anywhere 15% of the time spends about 31% of its time on A (1 in-link, from C) and about 33% on C (3 in-links), because a link from a busy page brings many visits, and that these long-run shares are PageRank.
